clue.text: Reinforce charge local stores reversed

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece is then read backwards
the pub stores the charge, i.e. holds it inside

parts.note: a local is a Briton's nearest pub
a charge or price is a fee

explanation.surface: An order to strengthen the fees a pub keeps, then undo them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' gives PUFEEB, which 'reversed' turns round. A 'local' is British slang for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something is to bulk it out or make it sturdier, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Spared one from Left becoming European Parliament member

indicators.note: the one is taken from the word for left and turns into the European Parliament member in its place

parts.note: left in the sense of went out, departed
one is the Roman numeral I
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone was let off when a left-winger turned into a Euro-MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' swaps the I in EXITED for E plus MP. The surface's 'European Parliament member' looks like an MEP, but E and MP are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spared means let off or excused from something, which is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Violence not a thing urban judge gets upset over

indicators.note: in a down clue the turned judge sits over, above, the following letters
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match
nothing, represented by the letter O
urban suggests the city, as in city life

explanation.surface: An urban judge gets upset over nothing much and turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' turns REF to FER; 'over' puts it above O and CITY in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery or fierceness is violence of manner, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Page ecofreak cobbled together that's impossible to read

indicators.note: cobbled together means roughly assembled, so the letters of ecofreak are rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmental zealot's page, crudely assembled, turns out illegible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobbled together' does the rearranging. The surface suggests a messy page; the definition means an expressionless face, not writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless look gives nothing away, so a card player's blank face cannot be read.

clue.text: Girl shut up youth? Sort of

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
pent means confined, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A girl kept confined has a youth of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by completing a phrase: 'misspent youth' is a familiar kind of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasted youth is the stock phrase, so the adjective names one sort of youth.

clue.text: Supplier of tablets, great when swallowed by day

parts.note: monumental means huge or great

indicators.note: the day takes in the word for when

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's great deal, gulped down by day.
explanation.walkthrough: The tablets are stone slabs such as headstones, not pills, despite 'swallowed by', which is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver of headstones supplies inscribed stone slabs, which can be called tablets.

clue.text: One at bridge with appropriate flood defence

parts.note: the four bridge players are North, South, East and West; S is South
and means with, together with
to bag is to take or appropriate

explanation.surface: A card player with the right means of keeping floodwater out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with sand are piled up against rising water as a barrier.

clue.text: You no longer row in the bar — finally one's got to make up

indicators.note: the old you and the row go inside the closing letters
finally picks the closing letter of each of the two words

parts.note: ye is an old form of you, no longer used
a line is a row

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned rower in a pub finally gets to make up after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and R from 'the bar', and 'in' sets the rest between them. 'make up' is cosmetics, not reconciling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic pencil for outlining the eyes is something used to apply make-up.

clue.text: Centrepiece in midnight rave's typically taking off

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the middle of the phrase that follows, its centrepiece

explanation.surface: The highlight of a typical midnight rave is everyone getting airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' sounds like a plane but means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A taking-off is a mocking imitation, and a grotesque parody is the same thing.

clue.text: A biker's fancy new helmet

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist's elaborate new crash helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges A BIKERS into BEARSKI. The helmet is a guardsman's tall fur cap, not a biker's.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur cap of British Guards regiments is ceremonial headgear, loosely a helmet.

clue.text: Article set before a girl

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A piece of writing placed in front of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Muscle swelling way beyond the normal range

indicators.note: the muscle makes the way swell by sitting inside it

parts.note: St is short for Street, a way
a pec is a chest muscle
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A bulging muscle outside the usual range of motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swelling' is the container signal. 'range' is the definition, not part of 'normal range'.
explanation.definitionFit: A full gamut or scale of values is a range, as in a wide range of opinion.

clue.text: Please press!

definitions.meaning: to please is to do someone a favour, accommodate them
to press is to compel or constrain someone

explanation.surface: A curt instruction, perhaps to an iron or a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to accommodate someone and to compel them, as in 'feel obliged'.

clue.text: Regime falling after trouble dispatching foreign currency

indicators.note: the falling piece comes after what is left of trouble
dispatching means getting rid of, so the currency is removed from the word trouble

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency
raining means falling, as rain does

explanation.surface: A regime collapsing after a crisis in which its currency was ditched.

explanation.definitionFit: A regime of exercise or practice is a course of preparation, as in fitness programmes.

clue.text: Some log in, prepared for the new term

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some students log in, ready for the start of the new school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' means a word, not a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word or expression recently invented is a newly made term.

clue.text: Many landed on beach then turned close to tiny tot

indicators.note: turned means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: to tot up is to add

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of tiny

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers flock to the beach, then a little child turns round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes ADD into DDA. 'tot' looks like a child but is the verb, to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: 6 June 1944, when Allied troops came ashore in Normandy, is the day meant.

clue.text: One's sweet daughter hung out with crooks

explanation.definitionFit: A ring of fried, sugared dough is a sweet, one of many.

clue.text: Since he died, old radio presenter's been included as well

indicators.note: the old presenter is included between the word for since and the death abbreviation

parts.note: ago means since, as in 'long ago'
ob., for Latin obiit, means he died, as on gravestones
a DJ, disc jockey, presents radio shows

explanation.surface: A late radio presenter has been in the news, as well since he died.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, from Latin obiit, is the abbreviation on gravestones; 'been included' sets the old presenter between since and he died.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's as well' and 'it's fortunate' are idioms with the same meaning, so these are interchangeable.

clue.text: In which perhaps cuffs get worn

parts.words: In which perhaps cuffs get worn

clue.text: Paper boxes charity event organised with bouquet

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

clue.text: Ace snapper lodging appeal, one causing a stir

clue.text: Idiot, say, that's housed free's last thing landlord needs?

clue.text: Top journalist's attempt messed up
